Class FileManager

java.lang.Object
FileManager
public class FileManager extends Object
Handles saving a Library to a plain text file and rebuilding a Library from that file. Keeping this logic in its own class means the model classes stay free of any knowledge of how they are stored on disk.

Each entry occupies one line, with fields separated by a vertical bar. The first field is always the media type label, which is what allows the parser to decide whether a line should become a Movie, a TVSeries, or a VideoGame: 

Movie|title|genre|status|rating|review|director|duration|releaseYear
TVSeries|title|genre|status|rating|review|totalEps|watchedEps|seasons
VideoGame|title|genre|status|rating|review|platform|specs|developer|hours

An empty rating field means the entry has not been rated. Any vertical bar or line break typed by the user is replaced with a space before writing, so that a single entry can never spill across field or line boundaries.

The target file name is not fixed for the lifetime of the object. MediaVault gives each user their own save file, so the controller repoints this manager at the appropriate file when a user logs in or signs up.

    • setFileName

      public void setFileName(String fileName)
      Points this manager at a different save file. Used when a user logs in so that each account reads and writes its own library.

      Precondition: fileName is not null
      Postcondition: subsequent saves and loads use the given file

      Parameters:
      fileName - the path of the save file to use from now on

    • buildFileNameFor

      public static String buildFileNameFor(String username)
      Builds the save file name belonging to the given username. Characters that are not letters, digits, or underscores are replaced so that a typed username can never escape the working folder or produce an illegal file name.

      Precondition: username is not null
      Postcondition: nothing is created on disk; only a name is built

      Parameters:
      username - the username to build a file name for
      Returns:
      the save file name for that user

    • fileExists

      public boolean fileExists()
      Reports whether the file this manager currently targets already exists. The controller uses this to tell an existing account from a new one.
      Returns:
      true if the save file exists, false otherwise

    • getSkippedLineCount

      public int getSkippedLineCount()
      Returns how many lines were skipped as unreadable during the most recent call to loadLibrary. A value of zero means the whole file parsed cleanly.
      Returns:
      the number of malformed lines skipped during the last load

    • saveLibrary

      public void saveLibrary(Library library) throws IOException
      Writes every entry in the given library to the save file, replacing any previous contents. Each entry becomes one delimited line.

      Precondition: library is not null
      Postcondition: the save file contains one line per entry

      Parameters:
      library - the Library whose entries should be written to disk
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file cannot be created or written to

    • loadLibrary

      public Library loadLibrary() throws IOException
      Reads the save file and rebuilds a Library from it. A file that does not exist yet is treated as an empty library rather than an error, so that the very first run of the program behaves sensibly. Individual lines that cannot be parsed are skipped and counted instead of aborting the whole load.

      Postcondition: a Library is returned holding every entry that could be parsed, and skippedLineCount reflects how many could not

      Returns:
      a Library containing every entry successfully read from the file
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file exists but cannot be read

    • parseEntry

      public MediaEntry parseEntry(String line)
      Rebuilds a single MediaEntry from one delimited line of the save file. The first field decides which subclass is constructed. A line with too few fields, an unrecognized type, a bad status name, or a non-numeric value in a numeric field is rejected rather than allowed to produce a half-built object.

      Precondition: line is not null
      Postcondition: nothing outside the returned object is modified

      Parameters:
      line - one delimited line read from the save file
      Returns:
      the reconstructed MediaEntry, or null if the line is malformed

    • formatEntry

      public String formatEntry(MediaEntry entry)
      Converts a MediaEntry into the single delimited line that represents it in the save file. The concrete subclass is identified with instanceof so that its type-specific attributes can be written after the shared ones.

      Precondition: entry is not null
      Postcondition: the entry is unchanged

      Parameters:
      entry - the MediaEntry to convert
      Returns:
      the delimited line representing the entry
